literal: others to-be-ashamed that-which-is-fit oneself is-not-ashamed if, virtue to-be-ashamed that-which-is-fit it-has.
translation: If a person is not ashamed of what makes others ashamed, virtue itself will find fit cause to be ashamed of him.
modern: பிறர் வெட்கப்பட வேண்டிய பழிச்செயலுக்கு ஒருவன் தான் வெட்கப்படாமல் இருப்பானானால், அறமே அவனைக் கண்டு வெட்கப்பட்டு விலகும் தன்மையை அது பெறும்.
explanation: This couplet defines true modesty as aligning one's moral compass with the conscience of the wider community. It warns that a person must feel ashamed of actions that others rightfully consider shameful. If someone brazenly commits such acts without personal shame ('தான் நாணான் ஆயின்'), they completely detach themselves from moral goodness. As a result, virtue ('அறம்') itself will feel ashamed to be associated with them and will abandon them.
